extracted.intended_audience: researchers and principal investigators preparing research grant proposals for the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research-project grant proposals to the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, including required elements, formatting, narrative sections, budget rules, appendices, and submission mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a Complete Grant Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: All grant proposals to the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation must contain the following elements: 1. Proposal Cover Sheet; 2. Proposal Narrative; 3. Participation & Engagement Plan; 4. Budget & Budget Justification; 5. Required Appendices; 6. Additional Appendices; 7. Proposal Administration Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals missing any of these elements are not complete and will not be considered for funding until all elements have been submitted. The first six elements should appear in a single document in the order indicated (cover sheet first, then narrative, then diversity plan, etc.). The Proposal Administration Form (element 7) should be submitted as a separate document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be double-spaced, use an 11-point font, have 1-inch margins, and include page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section Page Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of a grant proposal may not exceed specified lengths (e.g., Cover Sheet 1 page; Proposal Narrative 15 pages if request ≤ $250,000, 20 pages if > $250,000; Participation & Engagement Plan as needed, generally 2 pages; CVs 3 pages per person; Empirical Methods generally 3–8 pages; Information Products generally 2–4 pages; Letters of Support 2 pages per letter; Proposal Administration Form 2 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some items are listed 'as needed' and approximate; follow the specific numeric limits where given. The Participation & Engagement Plan does not count toward the 20-page proposal narrative limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Cover Sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: All grant proposals must be accompanied by a completed Proposal Cover Sheet Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download the form from the Forms section of the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation website. The Cover Sheet should appear first in the single-document submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Narrative — accessibility and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant proposal narrative must be divided into sections that address specified questions and should be written in a style accessible to an interested non-specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives are read by all senior staff and should be understandable to an educated non-expert. Write clearly and avoid unnecessary jargon; attach technical detail to appendices as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q1: Research question and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the research question and why is it important? The narrative should start with a discussion of the research question(s) the proposer expects to address and why these questions are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q2: State of the research / literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the state of the research on this question? The narrative should contain a concise summary of the existing literature and how the proposed project fits into, supplements, or extends that literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references to important papers (including key papers by the proposers and others), identify gaps in the literature, and show how the proposed work addresses those gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q3: Description of the research project, goals, and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the research project? What are its goals and its methodology? Provide a clear statement of the work to be undertaken, project goals, how goals relate to current research, and the research methods to be deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what proposers want to do, why, how they will know if they succeed, and expected benefits — written for an educated non-expert. Be explicit about critical assumptions, plans, and methods. Include theoretical frameworks, data sources, experimental equipment, analysis methodologies, and attach additional technical detail in an Empirical Research Methods Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q4: Key members of the research team
rubrics_metrics.description: Who are the key members of the research team? Introduce key members, the role they will play, and key accomplishments, training, or experience relevant to their role in a few sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include full CV-level detail here; detailed information (education, honors, publication history) belongs in the C.V. appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q5: Work plan and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the work plan? Discuss project timeline and implementation, who will do what and when, oversight and management, duties and responsibilities, key milestones, and success metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List collaborators and expected contributions, status of work to date if applicable, and plans for dissemination and/or sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q6: Anticipated outputs and success metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: What will be the output from the research project? Include anticipated publications, datasets, conferences, briefings, trainings, etc., and metrics describing what would constitute success (e.g., venues for publication, number of downloads, conference registrants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a general discussion in the narrative and attach a more thorough discussion in an Information Products Appendix where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q7: Summary justification for requested funding
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the summary justification for the requested funding? The proposer should justify the budget request and why it is consistent with the research and associated outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a general discussion in the narrative and include additional detail in the detailed budget justification appendix or section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q8: Other sources of research support
rubrics_metrics.description: What other sources of research support has the proposer applied for or have in hand? List other sources, amounts, and status of funding for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information can be integrated into the budget discussion and additional detail should be provided in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Q9: Status and output of current/previous Sloan grants
rubrics_metrics.description: For current or former Sloan grantees seeking new or renewed funding, include a discussion of work produced or in process connected with previous Sloan grants and a list of publications and other products designated as output or outcome metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include working papers, journal articles, books, dissertations, conferences, presentations, films, trainings, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation & Engagement Plan — overall principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sloan Foundation seeks projects that demonstrate a commitment and capacity to remove barriers that impede success in science and to foster inclusion and belonging; proposals must provide concrete plans to achieve these aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond a statement of commitment, the Foundation expects a specific plan and implementation strategies. This section does not count toward the 20-page proposal narrative limit. Proposers may include additional supporting materials in an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation & Engagement Plan — example content
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the project, the Participation & Engagement Plan may include items such as the project team's experience advancing access and opportunity; strategies to ensure an inclusive project environment; outreach and dissemination plans to reach underrepresented audiences; contributions to reducing barriers; mentoring philosophy and experience; collaborations with institutions serving students/communities facing barriers; and resources to support these strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit examples include listing institutional resources, mentorship plans, collaboration partners, and outreach approaches. The Foundation welcomes discussion of how these efforts align with the organization’s mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget & Detailed Budget Justification — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a tabular budget broken down by year for multi-year projects, followed by a detailed written discussion that explains and justifies the amounts requested and what line items cover and how they were derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation strongly recommends using the Foundation’s Project Budget Form to prepare the budget and ensure correct overhead calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary Support — faculty restrictions and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for faculty salary should adhere to restrictions based on type of staff. Definitions: 'senior faculty' = tenured or >10 years beyond Ph.D.; 'junior faculty' = non-senior faculty. Budgets must include number of faculty supported, full-time equivalent salary for each, and percentage of time devoted to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation discourages budget requests to pay summer salary for senior faculty. Proposals may request up to one month of summer salary for senior faculty equal to either 1/9 of academic-year salary or $35,000, whichever is lower, and must justify requests for junior faculty if different. For faculty on unpaid leave, modest academic-year support may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Staff salary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project/research staff may be supported as needed up to 100 percent of full-time salary. Budgets must list number of staff supported, the full-time salary of each, and percentage of time devoted to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All project/research staff employed by the grantee institution must receive a standard benefits package customary for their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Researchers support
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral researchers may be supported as needed up to 100 percent of full-time salary. Budgets must include number of positions, full-time salary of each, and percentage of time devoted to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Sloan-supported postdoctoral researchers must receive a standard benefits package customary for their institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate Students support and tuition policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate student support may be requested up to 100 percent of full-time salary. Budgets must include number of graduate students supported, full-time salary of each, and percentage of time devoted to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation strongly prefers funds for graduate students to be allocated toward salaries/stipends/direct support. If tuition coverage is requested, provide clear rationale; tuition reimbursement is capped at the NSF Graduate Research Fellow cost-of-education allowance (currently $16,000 per student per year). The Foundation does not pay indirect costs on graduate student tuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs / overhead policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For grant requests of $50,000 or less, no indirect (overhead) costs are permitted. For grant requests in excess of $50,000, indirect costs may not exceed 20 percent of direct project costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a subcontract, total overhead across grantee and subcontractor must not exceed 20 percent of direct project costs. Tuition is excluded from overhead calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract overhead splitting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a subcontract, proposers must split overhead costs with the subcontractor institution, with total overhead not to exceed 20 percent of direct project costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation suggests the grantee institution take 4% and assign the remaining 16% to the subcontractor (not a strict requirement). The Project Budget Form automatically calculates overhead on subcontracts; use it to minimize errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial plan for the whole effort
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total cost of the project is larger than the amount requested from the Sloan Foundation, include a financial plan for the whole effort that identifies other financial contributions (secured or anticipated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, include letters of support from other funders indicating willingness to provide funds and the amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Appendices — list
rubrics_metrics.description: All research project proposals must contain at least five appendices: List of Citations; Curricula Vitae; Conflicts of Interest / Sources of Bias; Empirical Research Methods; Information Products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appendices are required and should be provided as part of a complete grant proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Citations appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: This appendix should contain a list of all papers or other work cited in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations may be formatted in any widely used style (Chicago, APA, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricula Vitae appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Include abbreviated CVs or biographies of the principal investigator and any key project staff that will implement or supervise activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVs should include education, employment history, a list of the proposer’s most important previous publications, and important honors. Full CVs are not requested; one to three pages per person is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest / Sources of Bias appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal must disclose potential conflicts of interest or sources of bias for the PI, all key project staff, and the grantee institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of potential conflicts include significant financial interests (equity, stock options), management/advisory affiliations, paid consulting or honoraria within the last three years, and planned/pending/awarded patents with value tied to research outcomes. If there are no conflicts, include a statement to that effect rather than omitting the appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical Research Methods appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals requesting support for research must include a detailed methodological discussion written for an expert audience, similar in scrutiny to NSF panels or top research journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed technical information on research design, data/sample collection, instrumentation, approach to analysis and validation (power calculations, preregistration plans), structure/usage criteria for models, and qualitative methods' design and analytic approach. Include protocols (interview, survey, data collection) and describe protections for private/sensitive data and IRB review status. If producing data/models/code for others, list intended users and plans to make products meet their needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Products appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: List all information products expected from the project (articles, books, websites, datasets, software, instruments, etc.) and detail how each will be licensed, archived, shared, and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For articles/books: who holds copyright, license/archiving plans, preprint or repository plans. For datasets: where and in what format data will be archived and any legal barriers to sharing. For software: computational environment, sharing conditions, license, archive location, and maintenance plans. For instruments/hardware: documentation, licensing, commercialization plans, and access terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Appendices — workshops/conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting support for workshops, conferences, or large meetings, include appendices with: draft conference agenda; draft list of invitees with names/titles/affiliations; draft letter of invitation; draft list of speakers/panelists with names/titles/affiliations; draft call for papers (if applicable); draft anti-harassment policy; participant survey or evaluation plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference organizers should strive for diversity and inclusion (noting underrepresentation of Black, Indigenous, Latina/o/x, and women scholars) and are strongly encouraged to establish a formal anti-harassment policy. Include an evaluation plan (participant survey) to assess what participants valued and whether conference goals were met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project's success depends critically on support from key figures or institutions other than the PI or project team, include a letter from each such institution articulating the nature of their relationship to the project and their expected role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should state the institution’s understanding of their role in the project's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Administration Form (procedural mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: To process a successful grant proposal, submit a Proposal Administration Form as a separate document with administrative information about your institution (EIN, tax status, payment address, institutional contacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should include relevant contacts from the Office of Sponsored Research. For institutions with 170(c)(1) status, include the IRS letter documenting such. Submit the form ideally with the proposal or soon after to ensure prompt payment if awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Submit a Completed Grant Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant proposals invited by a Sloan program director should be submitted as an email attachment directly to the program director. If not invited, you may submit a Letter of Inquiry to the relevant program director via email per website guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Sloan Foundation website guidelines for Letters of Inquiry and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of Demographic Data on PI/Co-PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent to grant approval, the PI, Co-PIs, and key project staff will be emailed a form asking for demographic information (gender identity, country of origin, race/ethnicity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal information will be kept confidential and used to analyze grantmaking and assess commitments to access and opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality request
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation requests that prospective grantees treat grant proposals as confidential during the application process and refrain from publicly distributing proposals or disclosing their application status until the Foundation completes its evaluation and makes a funding decision.
